scope: Experimental fictional woodland environment. Six overlapping perspective reconstructions per viewpoint, not a recorded geographic panorama. Visual acceptance remains open.

assets.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Produce one high resolution texture atlas: exactly THREE COLUMNS and TWO ROWS, six perfectly square equally sized panels, no gutters, no borders, no text. Output 3072x2048 if possible. This is a cubical panoramic environment with overlapping perspective photos from ONE stationary camera. Each square panel is a rectilinear perspective projection with EXACT horizontal and vertical field of view 110 degrees. Camera axes form a cube, not a single stretched panoramic photograph. Top row: FRONT, RIGHT, BACK. Bottom row: LEFT, UP, DOWN. Image 1 is the front environment reference, images 2-5 are layout guides for right, back, left and down respectively; derive the straight-up sky/canopy view consistently from the other photos. Fix malformed geometry and discontinuities in the guides. Preserve recognisable natural layout and camera position. Front centered on muddy path, dense cattails right, willow bushes and fallen branches left; ground mossy stones at starting point, mud at path point or fallen branches at branch point. All six views are from the same camera center, only rotated exactly 90 degrees between cube axes, NO camera movement. Adjacent square faces overlap by 20 degrees: align identical twigs, stones, trunks and horizon in those overlap regions. Back must show ONE continuous coherent woodland return trail, never duplicate split paths or a vertical join. Up is a true straight upward rectilinear view of grey cloudy sky and willow canopy. Down is a true straight downward view of soil, moss and stones, no perspective swirl. Texture fine natural casual unedited phone photograph, overcast soft neutral light, irregular framing, no radial smear or fisheye, no CGI, no fantasy shine, no vignette. Top-row front photo and bottom-row left photo share precisely the same fallen branches and shrubs at their adjoining edges. Top-row front/right share precisely same cattails. Use the guides only to establish natural scene structure, do not reproduce their pasted bands, warping or seams. Six independent normal photographs correctly facing cube directions arranged in exact grid, no labels or UI.
